title: Dallas Weekend: Mavericks home opener, SMU-Cal and Stars-Islanders lead the Oct. 24-25 calendar
text:
Dallas Weekend: Mavericks home opener, SMU-Cal and Stars-Islanders lead the Oct. 24-25 calendar
SMU hosts California on Saturday morning, the Mavericks open their home schedule against San Antonio on Saturday night and the Stars host the New York Islanders on Sunday. A free Día de Muertos art exhibition at Crown Hill Memorial Park is open both afternoons.
Three home games at two Dallas venues lead the Oct. 24-25 weekend: SMU football hosts California on Saturday morning, the Mavericks play their first home game of the season against the San Antonio Spurs on Saturday night, and the Stars host the New York Islanders on Sunday at American Airlines Center.
SMU, 5-1 and third in the Atlantic Coast Conference, hosts California at 11 a.m. Saturday at Gerald J. Ford Stadium, with the game on The CW, according to ESPN. The Mustangs beat Virginia 23-13 at home on Oct. 17. California is 3-4 and lost 41-7 to Wake Forest in its most recent game, according to ESPN's California schedule.
The Mavericks host the Spurs at 7 p.m. Saturday in their home opener, the third straight season Dallas has played San Antonio in its first home game, according to FOX 4. The Mavericks open the season on the road at Houston on Oct. 21.
The Stars host the Islanders at 5 p.m. Sunday at American Airlines Center, according to the National Hockey League. Both teams entered the week with 4-3-1 records and nine points, according to NHL standings.
Away from the arenas, the Celebración del Día de Muertos art exhibition "Pathways of Past Lives: The Persistence of Existence" is open from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. both Saturday and Sunday at the Crown Hill Memorial Park mausoleum, with displays by local artists and an installation by Josh Niccolai-Belfi, according to the event's organizers. The celebration, run by Hughes Family Tribute Center, is free and open to the public, and the cemetery at 9718 Webb Chapel Road includes an Art Deco mausoleum recognized as a City of Dallas Historic Landmark, according to Visit Dallas. The celebration closes with an evening program on Nov. 2.
summary: Dallas Weekend: Mavericks home opener, SMU-Cal and Stars-Islanders lead the Oct. 24-25 calendar SMU hosts California on Saturday morning, the Mavericks open their home schedule against San Antonio on Saturday night and the Stars host the New York Islanders on Sunday. A free Día de Muertos art exhibition at Crown Hill Memorial Park is open both afternoons.
